accepted.s: The Andhra University Act received the assent of the Governor-General on:
accepted.x: The Governor-General gave assent to the Madras Act II of 1926 on 13 January 1926. The Governor had assented earlier, on 15 December 1925.
accepted.tq: Use the exact legislative sequence and distinguish the two assent dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925?
accepted.x: Education Minister A.P. Patro of the Justice Party introduced the Andhra University Bill on 20 August 1925.
accepted.tq: Test the person associated with the legislative action rather than the later university administration.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the original academic arrangement of Andhra University when it was established?
o: Headquarters at Vijayawada and teaching centre at Rajahmundry
Headquarters at Rajahmundry and teaching centre at Vijayawada
Headquarters at Anantapur and teaching centre at Tirupati
Headquarters at Visakhapatnam and teaching centre at Anantapur
accepted.x: At its establishment on 26 April 1926, Andhra University had its headquarters at Vijayawada and its teaching centre at Rajahmundry.
accepted.tq: Split the headquarters and teaching-centre details before selecting the exact pair.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The decision to locate the permanent seat of Andhra University at Visakhapatnam was taken in:
accepted.x: The seat was decided in December 1928 by Dr. Subbaroyan's ministry. The university was inaugurated at Waltair later, on 5 September 1930.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the decision date from the inauguration date.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Andhra University was inaugurated at Waltair on:
accepted.x: The university was inaugurated at Waltair on 5 September 1930, and Visakhapatnam became its present headquarters.
accepted.tq: Test the inauguration date independently from the Act and establishment dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was the Chief Minister at the time of the founding of Andhra University?
accepted.x: The Raja of Panagal, P. Ramarayaningar, was the Chief Minister when Andhra University was founded. It was created by the Justice Party government.
accepted.tq: Use the person-with-office trap by separating the founding ministry from later ministries.
accepted.sec: ■ Andhra University - establishment, Act, first headquarters, shift  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs regarding the Vice-Chancellors of Andhra University is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Cattamanchi Ramalinga Reddy was the first Vice-Chancellor from 1926 to 1931 and again from 1936 to 1949. S. Radhakrishnan served from 1931 to 1936.
accepted.tq: Match the office-holder with the complete tenure, including the interrupted second term.
accepted.sec: ■ Founding Vice-Chancellors - tenure  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: S. Radhakrishnan served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University during:
accepted.x: S. Radhakrishnan was Vice-Chancellor of Andhra University from 1931 to 1936.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between adjacent institutional tenures.
accepted.sec: ■ Founding Vice-Chancellors - tenure  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: C.R. Reddy selected Waltair for the university seat primarily because of its:
o: Political importance and proximity to Madras
accepted.x: C.R. Reddy chose Waltair for its climate and setting. He also coined the expression “City of Destiny” for Visakhapatnam.
accepted.tq: Identify the practical basis of an institutional-location decision rather than its political consequences.
accepted.sec: ■ Recommendation behind the shift of the seat  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched regarding the rival claims for the seat of Andhra University?
o: Anantapur — Rayalaseema claim and Senate vote of 35–20
Vijayawada — named as headquarters in the 1926 Act
Visakhapatnam — location finally rejected in December 1928
Rajahmundry — teaching centre and proposal associated with September 1928
accepted.x: Visakhapatnam was the final choice in December 1928, not a rejected location. Vijayawada, Rajahmundry and Anantapur had the other claims described.
accepted.tq: Find the single reversed outcome in a list of location-based associations.
accepted.sec: ■ Rival claims for the seat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Senate of Andhra University voted in favour of Anantapur as the seat by a margin of:
accepted.x: The Senate voted 35–20 in favour of Anantapur, reflecting the Rayalaseema claim. The Select Committee also endorsed Anantapur, although Visakhapatnam was finally selected.
accepted.tq: Use the exact vote margin as the deciding numerical clue.
accepted.sec: ■ Rival claims for the seat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What was one consequence of the amendment concerning Rayalaseema in the Andhra University arrangement?
o: Rayalaseema was excluded from the university's jurisdiction and its colleges returned to Madras University
Rayalaseema colleges were transferred to Osmania University
A separate university was immediately founded at Anantapur
The university was shifted permanently to Rajahmundry
accepted.x: An amendment excluded Rayalaseema from Andhra University's jurisdiction, and its colleges went back to Madras University.
accepted.tq: Test the institutional consequence of a territorial amendment.
accepted.sec: ■ Rival claims for the seat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Andhra members supported a no-confidence motion against Subbaroyan in August 1927 mainly in the context of the dispute over:
o: The appointment of the first Governor of Andhra
The seat and territorial jurisdiction of Andhra University
accepted.x: The Circars–Rayalaseema dispute over the university's seat and jurisdiction led Andhra members to support a no-confidence motion against Subbaroyan in August 1927.
accepted.tq: Link the political action to the underlying institutional dispute.
accepted.sec: ■ Rival claims for the seat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha, held on 28 January 1934, demanded:
o: A university at Tirupati and opposition to inclusion in Andhra University
The inclusion of Madras city in Andhra State
The merger of Rayalaseema with Hyderabad State
The transfer of Andhra University to Vijayawada
accepted.x: The First Rayalaseema Mahasabha opposed inclusion in Andhra University and demanded a separate university at Tirupati.
accepted.tq: Combine the date, regional body and precise demand in one direct recall question.
accepted.sec: ■ Rayalaseema's grievance and Sri Venkateswara University  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the university-related provision of the Sri Bagh Pact?
o: A university was to be established only at Kurnool
University centres were promised at Waltair and Anantapur
Andhra University was to be shifted entirely to Anantapur
Sri Venkateswara University was to replace Andhra University
accepted.x: The Sri Bagh Pact of 1937 promised Andhra University centres at Waltair and Anantapur.
accepted.tq: Test the specific institutional compromise without confusing it with the later university at Tirupati.
accepted.sec: ■ Rayalaseema's grievance and Sri Venkateswara University  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who wrote “Maa Telugu Talliki,” recognised as the State song of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: “Maa Telugu Talliki” was written by Sankarambadi Sundarachari and is the State song of Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Use the author-work association, a common culture-paper pattern.
accepted.sec: ■ Telugu identity symbols - Telugu Talli song, Andhra Parishat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following cultural markers is correctly matched with its date or period?
accepted.x: Waltair Andhra Varotsavalu took place in December 1937. Andhra Abhyudaya Dinam was observed on Ugadi, 24 March 1936; Diwali 1937 was marked as Andhra State Day; the Telugu-medium resolution dates to 1915.
accepted.tq: Match each cultural marker with its correct date and reject the swapped-date distractors.
accepted.sec: ■ Telugu identity symbols - Telugu Talli song, Andhra Parishat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who organised the Andhra Week during the Waltair Andhra Varotsavalu of December 1937?
o: The Justice Party government under the Raja of Panagal
The Madras Cabinet under P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja
accepted.x: The Andhra Week was conducted by students under the Vice-Chancellor C.R. Reddy during the Waltair Andhra Varotsavalu in December 1937.
accepted.tq: Identify the organisers and supervising authority in a cultural event.
accepted.sec: ■ Telugu identity symbols - Telugu Talli song, Andhra Parishat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which work is associated with Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao in the context of Telugu cultural identity?
o: On the Present Position of the Telugu People
accepted.x: Chilukuri Veerabhadra Rao wrote Andhrula Charitra, which is listed among the cultural markers of the Andhra movement.
accepted.tq: Apply the author–work matching method.
accepted.sec: ■ Telugu identity symbols - Telugu Talli song, Andhra Parishat  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Who was the leading champion of Andhra separation among the Madras Chief Ministers listed below?
accepted.x: T. Prakasam, Chief Minister during 1946–47, was the leading champion of Andhra separation and submitted a separate report to the Partition Committee.
accepted.tq: Match the political stand with the correct Chief Minister and tenure.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which Madras Chief Minister chaired the Partition Committee constituted in 1949?
accepted.x: P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja, Chief Minister of Madras from 1949 to 1952, chaired the Partition Committee.
accepted.tq: Use the office-holder trap by separating the committee chairman from the committee members.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about C. Rajagopalachari's position is correct?
o: He was the leading champion of a separate Andhra during 1946–47.
As Premier in 1937, he included Rayalaseema in his cabinet and supported Andhra separation.
As Premier in 1937, he left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet and later made anti-Andhra statements.
He chaired the Andhra Partition Committee and submitted a separate Andhra report.
accepted.x: C. Rajagopalachari left Rayalaseema out of his cabinet as Premier in 1937 and later made anti-Andhra statements. He served as Madras Chief Minister from 1952 to 1954.
accepted.tq: Use the person-with-deed trap and identify the precise political position.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Madras Partition Committee:
1. It was set up after the JVP report.
2. It met under the chairmanship of P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja.
3. It was constituted by the Madras Cabinet on 7 December 1949.
4. Its report was submitted on 4 January 1950.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The committee was formed after the April 1949 JVP report, constituted by the Madras Cabinet on 7 December 1949, chaired by Kumaraswamy Raja, and reported on 4 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Verify the committee through its origin, chairmanship, constitution date and report date.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT a task of the Madras Partition Committee?
o: Drafting the Constitution of the Republic of India
Consideration of the six Bellary taluks
accepted.x: The committee dealt with division of assets, administrative arrangements and the six Bellary taluks. Drafting the Constitution of India was not its task.
accepted.tq: Find the unrelated constitutional function among the committee's administrative responsibilities.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the Andhra members of the Madras Partition Committee?
o: T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy
T.T. Krishnamachari, Bhaktavatsalam, Madhava Menon and C. Rajagopalachari
P.S. Kumaraswamy Raja, T. Prakasam, Rajaji and N. Sanjiva Reddy
Kala Venkatrao, Bhaktavatsalam, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Madhava Menon
accepted.x: The Andhra members were T. Prakasam, Kala Venkatrao, Bezawada Gopala Reddy and Neelam Sanjiva Reddy. The other named members belonged to the Tamil side or chaired the committee.
accepted.tq: Separate the two regional groups before selecting the complete membership set.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Madras Partition Committee agreed that Andhra State should be formed on:
accepted.x: The committee's report of 4 January 1950 agreed on forming Andhra State on 26 January 1950, but that recommendation was not implemented.
accepted.tq: Distinguish a recommended date from the date on which the state was actually formed.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What was the principal difference between T. Prakasam's position and the majority position in the Partition Committee?
o: Prakasam supported Madras as the capital, while the committee rejected Andhra State altogether.
Prakasam opposed any separate Andhra, while the committee supported it.
Prakasam demanded Rayalaseema be excluded, while the committee demanded its merger with Hyderabad.
Prakasam wrote a separate report, while the committee otherwise agreed on forming Andhra on 26 January 1950.
accepted.x: The committee agreed on the formation of Andhra on 26 January 1950, but T. Prakasam submitted a separate report reflecting his distinct position.
accepted.tq: Compare the dissenting report with the committee's common recommendation.
accepted.sec: ■ Madras Chief Ministers before Andhra State - stand on separation  [APPSC, GROUP-II]

accepted.s: What did the Congress Working Committee recommend after the JVP report regarding the creation of Andhra State?
o: No linguistic state should be formed until after the States Reorganisation Commission.
Andhra should be merged with Rayalaseema and Hyderabad immediately.
Andhra should be formed without Madras city.
Andhra should be formed with Madras city as its capital and half the city shared with Tamil areas.
accepted.x: The Congress Working Committee recommended forming Andhra without Madras city. The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress accepted this position, while Andhra Congress wanted half of Madras town.
accepted.tq: Test the exact institutional recommendation and avoid confusing it with the Andhra Congress demand.
accepted.sec: ■ Congress Working Committee decisions after the JVP report  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the positions after the JVP report?
o: The Andhra Congress accepted the CWC recommendation without any reservation.
All Congress groups rejected the formation of Andhra State.
The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress agreed to Andhra without Madras, while Andhra Congress sought half of Madras town.
The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress supported Andhra with half of Madras city.
accepted.x: The Madras government and Tamil Nadu Congress agreed to the formation of Andhra without Madras city. The Andhra Congress, however, demanded half of Madras town.
accepted.tq: Compare the positions of the three political formations instead of treating Congress as a single undivided position.
accepted.sec: ■ Congress Working Committee decisions after the JVP report  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded that Andhra State be formed by:
accepted.x: The Andhra Mahasabha demanded the formation of Andhra State by 26 January 1950.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the movement's demanded deadline from later actual reorganisation dates.
accepted.sec: ■ Congress Working Committee decisions after the JVP report  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The report of the Congress Working Committee split Andhra leaders broadly into which groups?
o: Prakasam and Ranga on one side; Pattabhi and Sanjiva Reddy on the other
Prakasam and Pattabhi on one side; Ranga and Sanjiva Reddy on the other
Rajaji and Prakasam on one side; Ranga and Kumaraswamy Raja on the other
Pattabhi and Rajaji on one side; Prakasam and Kamaraj on the other
accepted.x: The CWC report divided Andhra leaders into the Prakasam–Ranga group and the Pattabhi–Sanjiva Reddy group.
accepted.tq: Match the leaders into the two political groupings rather than testing them individually.
accepted.sec: ■ Congress Working Committee decisions after the JVP report  [GROUP-II]
